A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EDITPP. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, forecasting, sampling-efficiency, and runtime experiments, with detailed results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds hyperparameter ablations, inpainting comparisons, and qualitative sampling analyses in Appendices D and E.

M1.justification: The edit operations, alignment costs, training loss, Llama architecture, Euler sampler, and masked conditioning procedure remain unchanged. The added inpainting experiment uses the existing conditional sampler; expanded explanations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds inpainting across the seven retained real-world datasets, conditioning on both past and future events to generate a missing middle interval. This substantially extends evaluated conditional capabilities beyond forecasting. The thirteen original datasets remain unchanged; Appendix B documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: IFTPP, ADDTHIN, and PSDIFF remain the generation and forecasting comparators. Edit-count and runtime comparisons retain their respective comparator sets. The new qualitative comparisons use the same models, while inpainting compares conditioning settings of EDITPP.

E3.justification: Additional protocols compare past-only versus past-and-future conditioning for the fixed interval [T/3, 2T/3], sweep substitution distance and bin counts, and visualize 200 samples per model and process. Figure 4 adds MMD to the sampling-step evaluation. Original training budgets and primary evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sampling-step analysis, Appendix D adds sensitivity tests for substitution distance, insertion bins, substitution bins, and joint bin counts on PUBG and Twitter. Appendix E adds a conditioning-context comparison and event-raster/count-trajectory case studies, substantially expanding examination of design choices and generated behavior.

E5.justification: v3 adds variability values to the edit-count table, explicitly reports standard errors in the ablation figures, and specifies standard-deviation-based grouping for benchmark rankings. Both versions already report five training seeds and uncertainty alongside detailed performance scores; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: New ablation, inpainting, qualitative-sampling, and MMD-versus-step results substantially expand the evidence. Average edit totals change from 193.29 to 199.65 for EDITPP and 232.68 to 234.52 for PSDIFF, retaining EDITPP's advantage. All numerical entries in v1 Tables 6–11 match v3 Tables 7–12; new middle-interval results are not same-setting improvements over those forecasts.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 explicitly qualifies finiteness as almost sure and changes the survival-factor conditioning in Eq. (2) from H_t to H_{t^(i)}, leaving i unspecified outside the product. The method equations and alignment reasoning remain intact; expanded design explanations do not constitute new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous-time edit modeling, conditional flexibility, competitive generation and forecasting, and reduced edit operations. Added experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1 newly interprets the inpainting comparison as demonstrating the value of future context for reconstructing a missing middle segment. Existing explanations of forecasting error accumulation and edit efficiency remain, with no substantive new limitations discussion.

D1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands documentation of retained datasets through generator formulas and parameters, provenance, collection periods, sequence counts, time supports, and summary statistics. The first page also adds a code-access pointer. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed datasets or training configurations.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion retain the same works and positioning relative to autoregressive TPPs, diffusion-based set interpolation, and Edit Flows. Additional dataset descriptions cite works already present in v1.

P1.justification: v3 clarifies blank-token removal, boundary padding, operation uniqueness, and alignment validity. It reorganizes the appendices into dedicated data, metrics, ablation, and results sections and adds acknowledgments. Most main-text wording and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds sensitivity plots, event rasters, cumulative-count plots, a dataset-summary table, and an inpainting table. Figure 4 expands from two panels to three. The edit-count table gains uncertainty entries, benchmark highlighting changes, and existing displays are relocated within the expanded document.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the paper easier to assess and reproduce through dataset documentation, a code pointer, sensitivity tests, and direct evidence of inpainting capability. These usefully supplement the already substantial benchmark evidence in v1. Unexplained edit-count revisions, limited interpretation of the ablations, and the new indexing ambiguity in Eq. (2) temper the improvement.
